pr_title: [release/7.0] Close MsQuic after checking for QUIC support to free resources (#75163, #75441)
pr_body:
Manual backport of #75163 and #75441
Fixes #74629
Replaces #75330 

cc: @wfurt 

## Customer Impact

Memory (and number of processes) regression in .NET 7.0 from .NET 6.0 for all applications (on Win11+/Win2022+ and Linux with OpenSsl 1.1):
Even if app is not using HTTP/3 (or QUIC), we initialize early on native MsQuic.dll which always allocates threads (2* number of logical cores). Thus, causes unnecessary resource increase even if the process does not end up using HTTP/3 at all (HTTP/3 is opt-in like HTTP/2).

The fix closes all MsQuic resources after their initialization.
The change builds on fix in msquic 2.1.1 (Helix images were updated by PR #75479).

Affected platforms include Windows 11, Windows Server 2022, many Linux platforms with msquic package installed. 

Note: The same problem exists also in 6.0, but hidden under opt-in switch into HTTP/3 support. We had 1 customer with ~50-core machine who noticed that in a dump and were surprised to see so many extra threads they didn't know about / they didn't need. At minimum it will help avoid developer confusion in dump investigations in such cases.

## Testing

Functional tests suite passes as part of the CI, resource consumption was checked manually.

## Risk

Low, the fix consists of gracefully de-initializing MsQuic library in the process after checking QUIC support. The library is re-initialized only when actually needed.

issue_context.title: HttpClient creates Quic threads even if HTTP/3 is not in use
issue_context.body:
1. Create simple console app with HTTP and run simple http1.1 request  on Windows 11 or Server 22. 
2. look at application threads.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/14356188/186841698-87e4f329-335e-4fa2-971f-28d8f92a7bcd.png)

Application crates 2x threads per core even if HTTP/3 and Quic are not in used. This was originally reported on legacy system with 54 cores. That will create 100+ threads ... for nothing. 

We should figure out how to make `Quic.IsSupported` cheap and defer thread creation until needed. 
This will impact legacy app that has no clue tor intention to use Quic or HTTP/3.

Triage: This contributes to 1MB per core Working set regression on Windows 2022/Win11+ and on Linux when msquic is present.
We should fix it in 7.0.

I talked with Nick in MsQuic discord about this, `MsQuicOpenVersion` will allocate threads for handling UDP sockets, this is being made lazy by https://github.com/microsoft/msquic/pull/3034, and another set of threads is allocated by `RegistrationOpen`.

One direction they consider moving is allowing applications (in our case, .NET Runtime) completely control the threads/scheduling, but that is distant future. 

Closing MsQuic via `MsQuicClose` after checking for support and later opening it again lazily when needed is currently the best option.
Is it worth of picking up that change? It seems like we can suppress the ongoing thread cost but we would still create and destroy the threads when checking the version...
That MsQuic PR is making API changes, which would prevent it from being ported to the release branch.
Reopening for backport
The change in 8.0 was reverted by PR #74984

This will need a change in MsQuic: https://github.com/microsoft/msquic/pull/3041, so backporting to 7.0 would require porting updated MsQuic as well, do we still want to do that? @karelz?

cc: @stephentoub

I think we can keep 2.1.0, it is, after all, the minimum required version. What do you think, @wfurt?

But I would expect that most people regularly update packages on their systems so most people would run with 2.1.1 anyway.

Reopening to track 7.0 backport.
@wfurt are we ready to start the backport, or are we blocked on other changes to msquic 2.1.1 deployment to our Docker images and into Helix?

From what I understand, the PR updates the relevant docker images to a version which works, and later, there will be another PR which updates to images to the official 2.1.1 bits on all tested platforms.
Based on discussion on the PR: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/75330#issuecomment-1243910432 ... we believe some fix should happen in 7.0 - either in RC2/GA or in servicing.
Reopening for 7.0 backport (though we may need to wait for more validation in main first).

Open questions:
- [x] Is #75493 regression caused by unloading msquic and will this change address it?
- [ ] CR feedback - take another look if we can avoid touching msquic more - https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/75330#issuecomment-1243921873
    - Will be discussed in team meeting with @stephentoub in presence
Fixed in main (8.0) in PRs #75163 and #75441 and in 7.0 (GA) in PR #75521 and in 6.0.15 in PR #80785.
We have customers impacted on 6.0 as well - only via Kestrel. Reopening for 6.0.x backport.

review_comments: Old version had `TryGetExport` for these methods, but what will happen now if the export fails? Will it throw? Will it return null?

`NativeLibrary.GetExport` will throw an exception when the export is not found in the library.

From https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/75441#discussion_r968487398 : The failures to get exports from the MsQuic library should be fatal. If we fail to get the export, it means that there is something very wrong.
